propositions: Reconciler re-attempts the same structurally-impossible inbound link ADDs (closed source, redundant ancestry, cycle) on every pass without any durable record of the failure, causing ~200 doomed writes per hour and permanent WARNING log floor.

Current applier (apply_inbound_records._inbound_update_apply_links) catches and logs link failures but stores no memory of the outcome; identical failures re-derive and re-attempt identically until local structure changes.

Link ADD failures classified as closed_source, redundant_ancestry, or cycle are deterministic structural verdicts raised by graph/_links.py::add_dependency, not transient I/O faults, and re-raise identically until the deciding local state changes.

A durable impossible_links.json store with deciding digests covering endpoint status, parent chain, and dep set allows the applier to skip already-failed ADDs; a structural change invalidates the record and permits one retry attempt.

Cycle records must key on the global structural projection (all tickets' status/parent/deps) because add_dependency walks the transitive graph; unlinking an intermediate ticket can break a cycle while both endpoints remain unchanged.

The endpoint fingerprint must cover the entire parent chain because resolve_hierarchy_link can redirect an endpoint to a type-tier ancestor before validators run; the deciding status may belong to the promoted ancestor, not the passed-in id.
